segments.visible_description: Hedy Lamarr sits at a film-studio worktable while illuminated set pieces and crew remain visible behind her.
segments.narration: You already know her face: the billed movie star and bombshell.
segments.editorial_purpose: Open on both the public film-star identity and the private worktable rather than an anonymous time-jump card.

segments.visible_description: Hedy draws a glowing signal path across a frequency diagram between film takes.
segments.editorial_purpose: Make the narration's switch from public image to active invention immediately visible.

segments.visible_description: Hedy studies the frequency-hopping diagram at the studio desk with a closed technical folder beside it.
segments.narration: Being underestimated; the war; radio-controlled torpedoes whose easy-to-find signal could be jammed.
segments.editorial_purpose: Hold a closer technical composition while the problem and her underestimated position are explained.

segments.visible_description: The encoded signal path moves across the frequency chart while the studio practicals remain restrained.
segments.narration: The signal hops from frequency to frequency and the receiver follows in step.
segments.editorial_purpose: Use the existing motion only for the process it actually depicts instead of treating it as generic Hedy coverage.

segments.visible_description: Comic emphasis card reading ‘You cannot jam a signal you cannot find.’
segments.narration: You cannot jam a signal you cannot find.
segments.editorial_purpose: Land the exact line in a short, legible beat.

segments.visible_description: The technical folder sits closed beside Hedy and her frequency chart on the studio desk.
segments.narration: Hedy and George Antheil presented the idea; the Navy called it too bulky and shelved it.
segments.editorial_purpose: Return to the visibly shelved technical work after the exact quote, not as a consecutive duplicate.

segments.visible_description: A memorial portrait surrounds Hedy with frequency-hopping diagrams, transmitter frequencies, film and wireless lineage symbols.
segments.narration: Frequency hopping sits in the family tree of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the wireless world; recognition came late and without payment.
segments.editorial_purpose: Shift from the shelved wartime idea to the long technical and cultural legacy the narration names.

segments.visible_description: Hedy remains alone at the film-set worktable while the star-marked studio continues behind her.
segments.narration: The most beautiful woman in the world—and nobody heard a single word she said.
segments.editorial_purpose: Return deliberately to the film-star frame for the final contrast between how she was seen and what was ignored.

required_gate: independent Hedy likeness and historical-detail review
independent judgment that the compressed signal motion remains natural
independent p21/p22 and p23/p24 transition review
